name: João Caldas
headline:
One curious mind.
A few different lives.
intro: Brazil, Sweden, Switzerland. Hacked computers, chased waves, ran Ironmans, then spent two decades making finance make sense in messy businesses. Now I’m wiring that curiosity back into AI, design and interactive worlds.
career: 20+ years across finance, financial planning, senior leadership and board-level work, alongside experience in marketing, sales and demand planning.
now: Over the last four years, AI has brought my early builder’s curiosity back into focus. After retiring from amateur triathlon, I’m bringing that energy into experiments with finance, design and interactive worlds.
basis: Life story provided by João. Employer history and responsibilities from his career CV; current Miele role and speaking appearances linked to public sources. Short descriptions summarise the work; they do not claim measured business results.

chapters.title: The hacker chapter.
chapters.text: My first short career was as a hacker. Computers were something to take apart, understand and experiment with—a curiosity that stayed with me after my focus moved elsewhere.
chapters.carry: What carries forward: a builder’s curiosity.

chapters.title: Then the ocean took over.
chapters.text: Surfing pulled my attention away from computers in the early 2000s. Later came amateur triathlon: Ironman 70.3 and full-distance races in different countries, alongside my business career. The friendships and people I met matter as much to me as the finish lines. I have retired from racing; the curiosity stays.
chapters.carry: What carries forward: practice, patience and feedback.
chapters.link: Explore the worlds shaped by sport

chapters.title: The other kind of endurance.
chapters.text: Finance and financial planning, senior leadership and board-level work, with experience across marketing, sales and demand planning. Different functions, connected decisions—and the need to understand the whole business.
chapters.carry: What carries forward: commercial context and a disciplined approach to decisions.

chapters.title: Now, connect the dots.
chapters.text: Living across Brazil, Sweden and Switzerland, working in different businesses, racing, surfing and meeting people gave me a lot of different ways to look at the same problem. Music, art and the unexpected belong in that mix too. AI now gives me a way to turn those connections into things people can try.
chapters.carry: What carries forward: all of it.

longBio: I collect hard problems: integrations that won’t reconcile, partners that don’t share systems, launches that look great until pricing hits reality, and plans nobody trusts by month three. The through-line is making the numbers useful in the room — then building the next thing when curiosity pulls harder than the last title.
shortBio: 20+ years across FP&A, systems, ops and Nordic leadership — Kraft → Mondelēz → Kao → Fox → Lavazza → Dyson → Miele — with sales and M&A chapters before that.
